subject: docs/coop/artifacts/doctor-actor-join-integration-contract.v3.json

shouldFix.title: The CA-1 repair narrows the component tail from all subsequent child effects to egress only
evidence: Both recorded host-effect generations state at /coveredActs/CA-1-host-head/subtypes[SPAWN] that the decision to spawn is the host head and 'The child's subsequent effects are DR-105.' The v2 predecessor carried the same broad boundary: the admitted child's subsequent effects, including egress, stay in DR-105.

V3 replaces that rule with only 'the child's subsequent component-originated egress is DR-105 / PT-NET-EGRESS', and FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL likewise tests egress only. The repair correctly types egress as PT-NET-EGRESS rather than doctor CA-4, but silently drops every non-network child effect from the named tail.

The named permission v2/v6 vocabularies contain six non-egress component routes in addition to PT-NET-EGRESS: PT-FS-READ-PROJECT, PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT, PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE, PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED, PT-ENV-READ, and PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED. A phase-exact join cannot leave those child effects outside the tail fixture.

The candidate's unchanged /identityDependencies/dependencies[ID-DEP-J3] still says 'Component tails stay there', while /honestyRepairsFromV1/0 still uses the superseded phrase 'component-originated CA-4 egress'. Those recitals do not restore an executable, typed fixture for the omitted effects and leave two incompatible descriptions in the same candidate.
The artifact applies nothing and the fixture classes are NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED, so no omitted child effect has yet been authorized. That bounds the defect to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A future fixture corpus can pass after testing only component network egress, while a spawned admitted child performs filesystem, environment, subprocess, state, or brokered effects without the DR-105 tail assertion. Those effects could then be misread as covered by the host spawn authorization.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Restore the broad rule that every subsequent effect of the admitted CA-1 child stays in DR-105, then type egress specifically as PT-NET-EGRESS and not doctor/host CA-4. Make FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL cover the general child-effect boundary plus representative egress and non-egress routes. Mark the inherited 'component-originated CA-4' history as superseded or restate it with the typed PT-NET-EGRESS correction.

shouldFix.title: The CA-2 denial route still treats DR-119 as the pending gate and omits the separately required later D-000 joint product/authorization decision
evidence: Both recorded host-effect v8 and v25 say every CA-2 execution is unexercisable in the architecture preview and that a later D-000 product/authorization decision owned by the DR-119 product owner jointly with Security+platform is required before any CA-2 becomes exercisable. They expressly make DR-119 necessary but not sufficient and forbid borrowing host CA-4 or PT-NET-EGRESS for the tool's sockets.

V3's CA-2 clause calls the later route '(DR-119, and DR-117/128 if third-party)'. FC-JOIN-CA2-UNEXERCISABLE says CA-2 remains denied 'pending DR-119', and ID-DEP-J4 rides only DR-119 plus the third-party rows. None names the mandatory later D-000 joint decision or tests the case where DR-119 exists but that decision does not.

The separate later D-000 decision is also absent from remainingNamedNotResolved. As written, FC-C1 plus DR-119 can be mistaken for sufficient admission even though every recorded host generation denies that interpretation.
CA-2 is still currently denied and no contract or fixture is applied, so the missing gate has not opened a live tool-execution path. That bounds the defect to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A future fixture can admit CA-2 after FC-C1 and DR-119 without the owner-recorded product/authorization decision required by both recorded host contracts, exposing an unbounded customer tool whose reads, writes, and sends OpenSIP cannot state.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Name the later D-000 product/authorization decision, with the DR-119 product owner jointly with Security+platform, as a separate necessary gate. State explicitly that DR-119 is necessary and not sufficient. Add a fixture case in which FC-C1 and DR-119 are present but CA-2 remains denied because the D-000 decision is absent, and list that decision under remaining unresolved work. Preserve DR-117/128 requirements for third-party cases and do not mint any grant.

advisories.title: The permission-v6 role recital still says it does not apply v2 inside the v3 artifact
advisories.observation: The inherited string reads 'Does not apply v2.' The enclosing standing and authority fields clearly say no named candidate is applied by v3, so the conclusion survives, but a successor-local recital should say 'this artifact' or v3.
